transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a little trouble keeping my answers straight when people ask me things. Like at work, someone will ask something simple, like when a ring repair will be ready, and I start answering, but then I somehow go from invoices to garden soil to mortgage papers, and… I can see their face change, like I’ve lost them.

I know that probably sounds odd. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. I just thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets more noticeable. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling unusually high or full of energy lately?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not unusually high, anyway. I mean, I have days where I try to push through and act more upbeat, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been full of energy or anything like that. Does that answer it okay?
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Um… not exactly voices like a conversation, I don’t think. But sometimes when the shop is really quiet, I’ll hear what sounds like a woman kind of muttering my name from the polishing room. It’s soft, and I usually tell myself it’s just the building or something.

But it feels real enough that I go check. And sometimes I smell burning metal when the torches are off, too, which… I know sounds strange. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a seizure?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, not that anyone’s ever told me. I’ve never had one of those episodes where I was shaking or blacked out, at least not that I know of. Is that what you mean by seizure?
Have you been noticing problems with your memory?

Not really, no. I mean, I forget little things sometimes, like where I set a tool down or why I walked into a room, but I think that’s pretty normal, right? I haven’t noticed anything major with my memory.
Have you been getting headaches?
No, not really. I mean, I get the occasional normal headache if I’m tired or I haven’t eaten, but nothing that’s been standing out to me or worrying me. Is that okay—like, is that what you’re asking?
Do you feel like someone is trying to harm you or spy on you?

I wouldn’t say harm me, exactly… I mean, I know this probably sounds odd. Sometimes I get this feeling that certain customers are coming in just to check up on me, like whether I’ll miss payments or something with the new showroom. They ask a lot of questions about it, and my husband says they’re just being friendly, so maybe I’m making too much of it. But it does feel like more than friendliness sometimes. Is that… does that make sense?
Have you been feeling depressed most days?

I guess… yes, most mornings, anyway. I try not to make too much of it, because I can still get myself going, but I wake up with this kind of flat, heavy sadness—like the color’s already drained out of the house before I even get to the shop. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you felt as if your thoughts were being put into your mind or taken out by someone or something?

Not like thoughts being put in or taken out, no… I don’t think so. It’s more that I get stuck on this idea about some customers, like they’re coming in and asking too many questions about the new showroom because they’re checking if I’ll miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, so I’m trying not to overreact, but it can feel very convincing at the time. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Did these experiences begin after any significant medical illness, head injury, or other change in your physical health?

Not that I can think of, no. I haven’t had anything like a head injury or a big illness that started it. I mean, I’m not always the best at noticing every little change, but nothing significant comes to mind. Is that what you mean?
Have there been times when the muttering voice or those suspicious feelings happened even when you were not feeling depressed?

Yes… I think there were times like that. It wasn’t as if I was in that heavy low mood yet—I was still running my classes and getting out in the garden, doing fairly normal things. But for a few weeks I kept hearing little noises from the polishing room, like someone was there, and I’d get worried that customers were watching the business too closely. I didn’t make a big fuss about it, but… yes, it did happen before the depression really settled in, if that helps.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes… a bit. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I used to really love hunting for old clasps and planning those little jewelry classes. Lately I’ll sit with the trays in front of me and just sort of stare at them, and it feels like… none of it is worth starting. Is that the kind of loss of interest you mean?
When you start talking and your answers drift from one topic to another, does it feel hard to keep your thoughts organized?

Yes… I suppose it does, though I try not to let it show too much. I came in partly because people would ask me something simple, like when a ring repair would be ready, and my answer would somehow start with the invoice, then I’d be talking about garden soil, and then mortgage papers… and I could see they were losing me.

I don’t mean to ramble on purpose. It’s just like the thoughts don’t stay in the right little compartments. Does that make sense?
Have other people noticed that your face or voice seem less expressive than they used to be?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my face being different, but I suppose I don’t always see myself the way other people do. My voice… maybe I’ve been quieter? No one has said it directly, though. If they have noticed, they’ve been kind about it. Is that what you mean?
For at least one month, have you had the muttering voice or those suspicious thoughts on most days?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but those things—the muttering voice, and the odd smells, and worrying customers were watching us—started maybe about a year and eight months ago.

It hasn’t been every second or anything, but on most days, yes, at least in some form. Is that the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or irritable for several days in a row?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I’ve had days where I felt a bit more on edge or irritable, but I wouldn’t call it unusually high or euphoric for several days. Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean.
